_comment: Asian board for the 2026-09-12 slate (Taipei 09-13). Twelfth slate of the prospective test. All fifteen games on the US card, all legible with first-half totals. The four-slate streak without a reading conflict ends here: Pirates at Cubs is corrected to Chicago. I read the handicap on Pittsburgh's row, but the market has the Cubs at 0.5325 with all fifteen books above even money and none below, so the moneyline decides and Pittsburgh is recorded as the alternative reading. The board prints no moneyline column for that game. Nine games do show one and all nine agree with the market, a streak that has still never broken. Of the other five games without it, four match my reading on the market alone -- Toronto 0.5409, Washington 0.5325, Atlanta 0.5549, St. Louis 0.5087 -- and the fifth, Guardians at Twins, is a 0 handicap sitting on a dead 0.5000 market, where laying and receiving are the same wager either way. Worth noting without leaning on it: the first-half handicap for Pirates at Cubs sits on Chicago's row, which is the reading the market confirms. That is the same row-mismatch pattern I withdrew as a tell yesterday after it went one for two; it is now two for three, which is still not evidence, and the rule continues to rest on the moneyline rather than on this. Handicaps flat at 0.950, totals flat at 0.940, no split prices.
